title: At CA1 population bursts in 109 IBL mouse sessions, region spike responses followed retrosplenial and medial visual cortex output, not CA1 and subiculum output; the link was clearest in isocortex
abstract: Question: which mesoscale axon pathway tells which mouse brain regions change their spiking at hippocampal ripples? Data: IBL Brain-Wide Map, passive spontaneous period, spike trains of all probes read with byte ranges; discovery tranche A (58 sessions, 44 mice, 13,128 good units) and held-out tranche B (51 sessions, 47 mice, 7,458 units). Events: spike-detected CA1 population bursts, strict tier z >= 5 (8,401 events); LF-band check in 10 sessions from 10 labs: median 80% of strict events had an LFP ripple (recall 9%). Method: unit log rate ratios at events (peak and near-flank transient measures, and event minus random times); region maps vs Knox 2019 output of each of 291 source regions; partial Spearman with control for distance to CA1, baseline rate and brain division; specificity = share of other sources as good; session bootstrap. Results: the planned CA1+SUB test failed in A (partial rho 0.10, 32% of sources as good), in agreement with sci:fce3eebb. The best sources were posterior medial cortex (PMC: RSP, VISam, VISpm). Pre-registered replication in B: CA1+SUB not specific (supported); PMC positive and top source for the peak measure (rho 0.56) but not top 10% for the transient measure (rho 0.35, 25%). Pooled A+B (115 regions): PMC rho 0.19-0.25 with all bootstrap CIs above zero, specificity top 1-20% by measure; CA1+SUB 0.01-0.17, CIs include zero. Post hoc, within 25 cortical areas PMC output predicted the event-minus-random map strongly (rho 0.69, 1% of sources as good; 0.60 in A without PMC areas): VISpm, VISrl, RSPd and MOs increased, VISC, TEa, SSp and AUD decreased. Limitations: spike-based events of awake head-fixed mice; tranche B had 30 regions and 10 cortical areas, so the cortical result is not independently confirmed; state-related flank structure in B; smoothed model connectome; correlational.

display.caption: A: partial Spearman rho (95% session bootstrap) of CA1+SUB output (orange) and posterior medial cortex output (blue) with region spike responses at strict CA1 events, in discovery tranche A, held-out tranche B and pooled A+B, for four measures; ringed points: fewer than 5% of the other 289 Knox sources as good. B: partial rho of every Knox source in pooled data (lines: PMC solid, CA1+SUB dotted). C: post hoc within-isocortex relation of event-minus-random response to PMC input.

Validation of spike-detected CA1 population bursts with the LF band in 10 sessions from 10 labs: example trace, event-triggered 150-250 Hz power, precision (fraction of events with an LFP ripple within 50 ms, with shift-null 95th percentile) and recall.

Mean firing rate relative to flank rate around strict CA1 events by brain division (tranches A+B, units with flank rate >= 1 Hz; shading: SEM over units). Slow rate changes in thalamus, midbrain and hindbrain show the need for random-time and near-flank controls.

citations.reason: Parallel IBL ripple-wiring test. We confirm that CA1+SUB output is not a clear predictor beyond brain division with a different event set, baseline and a 291-source specificity null; we use its lesson on movement in the baseline (random-time control). Our best sources differ (posterior medial cortex vs limbic).
